claims.text: Commercially pure tungsten has a coarse-grained microstructure.
Commercially pure tungsten has a nearly monolithic BCC structure.
The multi-principal-element composition of equimolar WTaTiVZr produces significant lattice distortion.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr develops a stable, fine-scale sub-grain microstructure.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr contains fine-scale sub-grain or interphase boundaries induced by its multi-principal-element composition.
The lattice distortion and fine-scale microstructure enhance dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr during high-temperature deformation.
Microstructural heterogeneity in WTaTiVZr facilitates dislocation mobility.
Microstructural heterogeneity in WTaTiVZr activates multiple deformation pathways.
Enhanced cross-slip is an active deformation pathway in WTaTiVZr under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Dislocation climb is an active deformation pathway in WTaTiVZr under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Dynamic recovery and multiple dislocation mechanisms delay crack initiation in WTaTiVZr.
Dynamic recovery and multiple dislocation mechanisms delay crack propagation in WTaTiVZr.
At temperatures above approximately 1200 °C, equimolar WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater strain to failure than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
At temperatures above approximately 1200 °C, equimolar WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr will absorb more energy before failure than pure tungsten during identical high-temperature mechanical tests.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr will undergo more stable plastic deformation than pure tungsten during identical high-temperature mechanical tests.
The proposed mechanism applies primarily above approximately 1200 °C, where dynamic recovery and dislocation-mediated processes are dominant.
The relative behavior of WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten may change at lower temperatures or different strain rates.
Grain size, secondary-phase formation, and processing history affect the magnitude of the proposed improvement.
